llm.summary: This Walmart data-collection skill is mostly coherent, but it needs review because it has unsafe credential handling and a script import path that can run unreviewed local code.

dimensions.detail: Network access to Dataify and environment-token use are expected for this purpose, but wait_for_task.py sends the API token in api_key query parameters for status and download requests, increasing exposure through URL logging.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: scripts/submit_dataify_walmart_products.py prepends a sibling ../../dataify-task-operations/scripts directory to sys.path before importing task_runtime, so an unreviewed local sibling module can shadow the bundled runtime and receive the API token.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill allows implicit invocation, reuses a saved DATAIFY_API_TOKEN, and can submit/poll paid remote Dataify jobs without a fresh confirmation for clear low-risk requests; the Chinese instructions also allow a token supplied in the user request despite later saying not to paste tokens into chat.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No automatic background service, startup hook, memory write, or destructive persistence was found; persistent token setup is user-directed, but the saved token is then reused for future jobs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The main instructions and submit script are Walmart-focused and validate Walmart URLs/domains, but the package also bundles broader Dataify business/search workflow code that is not described by the Walmart-only skill purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this only in a contained environment, do not paste API tokens into chat, rotate the token if it may have been exposed, and avoid running the bundled scripts until the external sys.path import is removed and task-status/download authentication no longer puts the token in URLs.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Partially accepted: the main Walmart submission path is purpose-aligned, but bundled generic business workflow and Dataify client code provide unrelated search, web-unlocker, lead, review, and brand workflows outside the declared Walmart scope.
[YR4] expected: Downgraded: the matched base64-like text appears in Walmart example URL parameters, not as exploit code or hidden instructions.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted for the bundled business_workflow.py capabilities, though not as evidence that the primary Walmart workflow automatically invokes them.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted as an overbroad bundled capability: lead discovery via LinkedIn/Crunchbase is not part of Walmart product collection, but it is not automatically executed by the documented Walmart path.
[LP3] expected: Network calls, shell execution, and environment-token access are expected for this integration, but the artifact does not tightly scope permissions around those sensitive actions.
[EA2] expected: Stored-token reuse is expected for a Dataify wrapper, but automatic continuation after token presence checks and low-risk defaults weakens user control over billable remote submissions.
[SQP-2] expected: Submitting Walmart parameters to Dataify is core functionality, but the instructions should more clearly warn that inputs are sent to a third party and may consume credits.
[SSD-3] unexpected: Accepted for SKILL.zh-CN.md: allowing tokens in the user request conflicts with safer local-environment guidance and can put secrets into chat history.
[SDI-4] expected: Downgraded: the dashboard-link guidance is inconsistent, but it is mainly a user-experience inconsistency rather than a standalone security issue.
[T07] unexpected: Accepted: the external sibling sys.path import can shadow the bundled task runtime and is not necessary for the declared Walmart task.
[T09] expected: Accepted: polling and downloading task results are expected, but placing the API token in query strings is avoidable sensitive credential exposure.
